publicDescription: The 2002-11-28 archived CanalBarra.com homepage included a direct webchat entry into Canal #barra with the nickname field pre-filled as guest_hp, alongside a warning not to use a registered nickname on public computers. The same homepage presented event coordination, event photos, an operators meeting reference, a 5th anniversary party callout and a best-cadastro voting module. Based on BarMan's founder/operator memory, this interface worked as an onboarding layer: visitors could enter the channel through the site, appear in Canal #barra under the recognizable guest_hp pattern, receive orientation from BarMan, learn how to use mIRC or regular IRC access, register their own nickname to preserve identity, and leave guest_hp available as a shared entry nickname for future visitors.

interpretiveClaims.claim: The pre-filled guest_hp nickname functioned as a low-friction visitor entry point from the website into Canal #barra.
The Brasnet-provided webchat acted as an initial onboarding bridge before some visitors learned to use mIRC or regular IRC clients.

BarMan states that he personally recognized guest_hp visitors inside Canal #barra as website entrants or newcomers, oriented them toward mIRC or regular IRC access, explained nickname registration as a way to preserve persistent identity, and encouraged them to stop using guest_hp so that the shared visitor nickname remained available for new people entering through the website.
The guest_hp flow created an onboarding path from anonymous or semi-anonymous website access into persistent nickname identity, community recognition and deeper participation in Canal #barra.
The homepage combined real-time channel access, event coordination, profile visibility, voting and community memory in a single public interface.
